history.summary: The generic 'Siddheshwara Temple [Warangal]' best matches the Sri Siddeshwara Temple at Meerpet, Hanamkonda - the Warangal-area Siddheshwara shrine. CSV town note: it is NOT in Warangal city proper but at Hanamkonda (Meerpet), part of the Warangal-Hanamkonda-Kazipet tri-city (~7 km from Warangal city); district is now Hanamkonda. The deity is a Swayambhu (self-emerged) Shiva between hills; the temple is noted as one of the few paschimdwara (west-facing) Mukha temples in India. A Kalabhairava figure is carved on a stone between two ~10-ft rocks in the temple's north-west backyard; Shiva-Parvathi images sit on the north-east side. A small pushkarini (tank) lies beside the temple, and the Padmakshi Temple stands on the opposite hill. Identity certainty: HIGH - this is the only Siddeshwara shrine documented in the Warangal/Hanamkonda area. ANTIQUITY CONFLICT: an INTACH/EBSB school-visit report says the temple was built in the 3rd century AD in Chalukya style, while Telangana exam references attribute the Hanumakonda Siddeshwara temple to Kakatiya king Prola Raja I - flag for verification.

name: Sri Siddeshwara Temple
town: Hanamkonda (CSV town 'Warangal' is approximate - the temple is at Meerpet, Hanamkonda, ~7 km from Warangal city, part of the Warangal-Hanamkonda-Kazipet tri-city)
town_description: Hanamkonda (Hanumakonda) is a major city and the headquarters of Hanamkonda district in Telangana, about 7 km from Warangal city in the Warangal-Hanamkonda-Kazipet tri-city. The Siddeshwara temple sits among rocky hills between Hanamkonda and the Padmakshi hill, in a scenic, lightly-visited precinct with a small tank beside the shrine.
